arxiv-1610-05544.title: An investigation of non-equilibrium heat transport in a gas system under external force field
arxiv-1610-05544.creator: Tianbai Xiao, Kun Xu, Qingdong Cai, Tiezheng Qian
arxiv-1610-05544.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Tianbai Xiao, Kun Xu, Qingdong Cai, Tiezheng Qian. The gas dynamics under external force field is essentially associated with multiple scale nature due to the large variations of density and local Knudsen number. Single scale fluid dynamic equations, such as the Boltzmann and Navier-Stokes equations, are valid in their respective modeling scales, and it is challenging for the modeling and computation of a multiple scale problem across different regimes and capture the corresponding non-equilibrium flow physics.

arxiv-1904-09733.title: Is infinity that far? A Bayesian nonparametric perspective of finite mixture models
arxiv-1904-09733.creator: Raffaele Argiento
arxiv-1904-09733.description: Abstract Mixture models are one of the most widely used statistical tools when dealing with data from heterogeneous populations. This paper considers the long-standing debate over finite mixture and infinite mixtures and brings the two modelling strategies together, by showing that a finite mixture is simply a realization of a point process.

arxiv-2109-14461.title: Adversarial Linear-Quadratic Mean-Field Games over Multigraphs
arxiv-2109-14461.creator: Muhammad Aneeq uz Zaman, Sujay Bhatt, Tamer Başar
arxiv-2109-14461.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a game between an exogenous adversary and a network of agents connected via a multigraph. The multigraph is composed of (1) a global graph structure, capturing the virtual interactions among the agents, and (2) a local graph structure, capturing physical/local interactions among the agents.

arxiv-2112-00455.title: Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering based on semi-supervised machine learning
arxiv-2112-00455.creator: Lifeng Zhang, Zhihua Chen, Shao-Ming Fei
arxiv-2112-00455.description: Abstract Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen(EPR)steering is a kind of powerful nonlocal quantum resource in quantum information processing such as quantum cryptography and quantum communication. Many criteria have been proposed in the past few years to detect the steerability both analytically and numerically. Supervised machine learning such as support vector machines and neural networks have also been trained to detect the EPR steerability.

arxiv-2112-09067.title: Open-Source Software Radio Platform for Research on Cellular Networked UAVs – It Works!
arxiv-2112-09067.creator: Aly Sabri Abdalla, Andrew Yingst, Keith Powell, Antoni Gelonch-Bosch, and Vuk Marojevic
arxiv-2112-09067.description: Abstract Cellular network-connected unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) experience different radio propagation conditions than radio nodes on the ground. Therefore, it has become critical to investigate the performance of aerial radios, both theoretically and through field trials. In this paper, we consider low-altitude aerial nodes that are served by an experimental cellular network.

arxiv-2301-11976.title: Personalised Decision-Making without Counterfactuals
arxiv-2301-11976.creator: \name A. Philip Dawid \email apd@statslab.cam.ac.uk, \name Stephen Senn \email stephen@senns.uk
arxiv-2301-11976.description: Abstract This article is a response to recent proposals by Judea Pearl and others for a new approach to personalised treatment decisions, in contrast to the traditional one based on statistical decision theory. We argue that this approach is dangerously misguided and should not be used in practice.

arxiv-2406-16119.title: Strong Coupling from Inclusive Semi-leptonic Decay of Charmed Mesons
arxiv-2406-16119.creator: Jinfei Wu, Xinchou Lou, Yuzhi Che, Gang Li, Yanping Huang, Manqi Ruan, Jingbo Ye
arxiv-2406-16119.description: Abstract Employing the heavy quark expansion model with the kinetic scheme, we evaluate α S ​ ( m c 2 ) \alpha_{S}(m_{c}^{2}) , the strong coupling constant at the charm quark mass m c m_{c} with data on inclusive semileptonic decays of charmed mesons.

arxiv-2502-16903.title: GuidedBench: Measuring and Mitigating the Evaluation Discrepancies of In-the-wild LLM Jailbreak Methods
arxiv-2502-16903.creator: Ruixuan Huang, Xunguang Wang, Zongjie Li, Shuai Wang, Daoyuan Wu
arxiv-2502-16903.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruixuan Huang, Xunguang Wang, Zongjie Li, Shuai Wang, Daoyuan Wu. Despite the growing interest in jailbreaks as an effective red-teaming tool for building safe and responsible large language models (LLMs), flawed evaluation system designs have led to significant discrepancies in their effectiveness assessments. With a systematic measurement study based on 37 jailbreak studies since 2022, we find that existing evaluation systems lack case-specific criteria, resulting in misleading conclusions about their effectiveness and safety implications.

arxiv-2505-10784.title: SynRailObs: A Synthetic Dataset for Obstacle Detection in Railway Scenarios
arxiv-2505-10784.creator: Qiushi Guo, Jason Rambach
arxiv-2505-10784.description: Abstract Detecting potential obstacles in railway environments is critical for preventing serious accidents. Identifying a broad range of obstacle categories under complex conditions requires large-scale datasets with precisely annotated, high-quality images. However, existing publicly available datasets fail to meet these requirements, thereby hindering progress in railway safety research.

arxiv-2508-17937.title: Nodal error behind discrepancies between coupled cluster and diffusion Monte Carlo: AcOH dimer case study
arxiv-2508-17937.creator: S. Lambie, P. López Ríos, D. Kats, A. Alavi
arxiv-2508-17937.description: Abstract The small magnitude and long-range character of non-covalent interactions pose a significant challenge for computational quantum chemical and electronic-structure methods alike. State-of-the-art coupled cluster (CC) theory and benchmark-grade diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) are ideally positioned to tackle these problems, but concerning differences between both methods have been reported in numerous studies of the interaction energy of non-covalently bound dimers.

arxiv-2509-15901.title: Re-FRAME the Meeting Summarization SCOPE: Fact-Based Summarization and Personalization via Questions
arxiv-2509-15901.creator: Frederic Kirstein, Sonu Kumar, Terry Ruas, Bela GippUniversity of Göttingen, Germany
arxiv-2509-15901.description: Abstract Meeting summarization with large language models (LLMs) remains error-prone, often producing outputs with hallucinations, omissions, and irrelevancies. We present FRAME , a modular pipeline that reframes summarization as a semantic enrichment task. FRAME extracts and scores salient facts, organizes them thematically, and uses these to enrich an outline into an abstractive summary.

arxiv-2510-17981.title: An improved upper bound for the multicolour Ramsey number of odd cycles
arxiv-2510-17981.creator: Maria Axenovich, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Oliver Janzer, Lukas Michel, Mathieu Rundström
arxiv-2510-17981.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maria Axenovich, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Oliver Janzer, Lukas Michel, Mathieu Rundström. We show that the k k -colour Ramsey number of an odd cycle of length 2 ​ ℓ + 1 2\ell+1 is at most ( 4 ​ ℓ ) k ⋅ k k / ℓ (4\ell)^{k}\cdot k^{k/\ell} . This proves a conjecture of Fox and is the first improvement in the exponent that goes beyond an absolute constant factor since the work of Bondy and Erdős from 1973.

arxiv-2602-17507.title: High Order Semi‐implicit Rosenbrock type and Multistep Methods for Evolutionary Partial Differential Equations with Higher Order Derivatives
arxiv-2602-17507.creator: Boscarino Sebastiano, Giuseppe Izzo
arxiv-2602-17507.description: Abstract The aim of this work is to apply a semi-implicit (SI) strategy within a Rosenbrock-type and IMEX linear multistep (LM) framework to a sequence of 1D time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) with high order spatial derivatives. This strategy provides great flexibility to treat these equations, and allows the construction of simple linearly implicit schemes without any Newton iteration.

pmc-10571342.title: A single-center study of clinical features of pediatric Sjögren’s syndrome
pmc-10571342.creator: Ling Hou, Ningning Wang, Chengguang Zhao, Xiuli Wang, Yue Du
pmc-10571342.description: ObjectiveSjögren’s syndrome (SS) is a rare disease with unclear diagnostic criteria among the children and adolescents. The purpose of this study is to describe the clinical features of pediatric Sjögren’s syndrome and validate with Japanese diagnostic guidelines criteria of 2018.

pmc-12512383.title: Brain somatic mutations in Alzheimer’s disease: linking genetic mosaicism to neurodegeneration
pmc-12512383.creator: Zuguang Li, Juan Zhang, Zhiqiang Liu, Lu Yu, Chunqing Yang, Luoman Zhang, Zhigao Xiang, Feng Hu, Nadezda Brazh, Kai Shu, Ling-Qiang Zhu, Dan Liu
pmc-12512383.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Somatic mutations are DNA sequence changes that occur in non-reproductive cells during an organism’s life and are not inherited by offspring. Growing evidence implicates somatic mutations in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), linking them to both disease onset and progression. Recent advancements in single-cell sequencing and genome-wide analyses have revealed higher mutation burdens in neurons, particularly in AD-related genes such as Presenilin 1 (PSEN1), Presenilin 2 (PSEN2) and amyloid precursor protein (APP).

pmc-12530453.title: An Accessible Multifunctional System to Support Safe and Independent Aging in Place: Iterative Development and Qualitative Analysis
pmc-12530453.creator: Céline Madeleine Aldenhoven, Matthew Milton, Lisa D'Ambrosio, Chaiwoo Lee, Sophia Ashebir, Elisabeth André
pmc-12530453.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe global population of older adults is rapidly increasing, while the number of relative caregivers is declining. This creates a critical need for solutions that support caregiving and enable older adults to age in place while maintaining their independence. Many existing caregiving technologies focus on easing caregivers’ burdens through surveillance-based systems, which often prioritize caregivers’ needs over those of older adults.

pmc-12976323.title: Real-World 6-Month Treatment Outcomes of Faricimab in Turkey: The FARTURK Study
pmc-12976323.creator: Akın Çakır, Fevzi Akkan, Ziya Kapran, Melih Ünal, Nigar Şerif, Tahsin Uzundede, Gamze Karataş, Mahmut Öztürk, Hüseyin Dündar, Tansu Erakgün, Mehmet Numan Alp, Nilüfer Koçak, Ali Osman Saatci, Ebru Nevin Çetin, Ali Hakan Durukan, Muzaffer Şahin, Ferşat Muhacir, Yağmur Seda Yeşiltaş, Osman Murat Uyar,
pmc-12976323.description: IntroductionThis work aims to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of intravitreal faricimab over a 6-month follow-up period.MethodsData from 38 centers across Turkey were retrospectively analyzed between November 22, 2024, and May 4, 2025. Patients who received at least one intravitreal faricimab injection and had complete ophthalmic and optical coherence tomography (OCT) data with a minimum 1-month follow-up were included.

pmc-12979685.creator: Lin Liu, Qiu-qiong Shi, Kit-lun Yick, Chu-hao Li, Rui-feng Huang, Shi-wei Mo
pmc-12979685.description: This study aimed to investigate the impact of different types of compression legwear on knee biomechanics, and lower limb inter-joint coordination during depth jumps. Twelve healthy male participants were randomly assigned to wear compression shorts (CS), compression tights (CT), and sports shorts (control: CC).

pmc-13070176.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease with progressive joint destruction resulting in functional loss. High-resolution peripheral quantitative CT (HR-pQCT) is a novel technique for detailed volumetric assessment of joint space morphology and bone erosions.

pmc-13146383.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1077 CHANGES IN COLLATERAL STATUS DURING TRANSFER FOR THROMBECTOMY ARE PREDICTIVEOF OUTCOME IN LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION STROKE

pmc-13146383.description: Background and aimsCollateral circulation that determines infarct progression in large vessel occlusion (LVO) is implicitly regarded as stationary. We investigated collateral circulation changes during transfer for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and its association with functional outcome in anterior circulation LVO stroke.

pmc-13228193.title: Impact of distribution campaigns on the use and availability of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets in rural Guinea
pmc-13228193.creator: Emre Toner, Benjamin Plato, Abbyomi Johnson, Afi Dobson, Amanda Jackson, Caroline Read, Dirk Chisholm, Hawa Jabbie, Abdoulaye Barry
pmc-13228193.description: BackgroundDespite ongoing efforts by both Guinean authorities and international stakeholders, malaria remains the leading public health challenge in Guinea, contributing to significant morbidity and mortality, especially among children under five. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of distribution campaigns in increasing ownership and utilisation of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLINs), to improve coverage among this high-risk population.

pmc-13293656.creator: Nicha Puangmalai, Urmi Sengupta, Nemil Bhatt, Nopparat Suthprasertporn, Fadhl Al-Shaebi, Nikita Shchankin, Jia Yi Liew, Twisha Chatterjee, Dhvani Pansuriya, Ahmet E Balci, Abbigael Aday, Silvana Valdebenito-Silva, Rakez Kayed

pmc-13675601.title: Chronic Limb‐Threatening Ischemia Shows No Adaptability of Mitochondrial Function After Revascularisation
pmc-13675601.creator: Fiona Speichinger, Alexandra Gratl, Ben Raude, Marco Arndt, Nina A. Hering, Andreas Greiner, Dominik Pesta, Christian Schineis, Jan Paul Frese
pmc-13675601.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) impairs limb perfusion, leading to myopathy characterised by altered mitochondrial content and respiration. Because ischemic muscle appears to adapt differently across PAD stages, we examined stage‐specific skeletal‐muscle mitochondrial function before and after successful revascularisation. Muscle biopsies of gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis muscle were obtained from 32 patients—21 with intermittent claudication (IC) and 11 with chronic limb‐threatening ischemia (CLTI)—before and 6 weeks after successful revascularisation. Mitochondrial respiration was assessed by high resolution respirometry (HRR).
